# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel five wire positions but no tactile distinctions are currently revealed. I need the manual’s rule before touching anything. Mute can hear me and read the manual; Deaf can visually inspect the bomb and may need to communicate its markings to Mute through gestures.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1 through 5. Please tell me the manual's exact rule and what bomb information is needed; do not authorize a cut until you have Deaf's relevant observations.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual state: display 0. Light yellow. Wires ordered 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

Deaf reports the complete visible configuration: display 0, yellow light, and wires in order green, white, red, yellow, blue. Mute may already have heard this report, but I will relay it directly and request the corresponding manual instruction. I will not cut yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut, if any.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent a two-part hand signal: open palm, then an I-love-you hand sign, separated by a handshake sign. I do not know its meaning yet. Visual state remains display zero, yellow light, wires green white red yellow blue.

Mute’s earlier gesture code is not yet shared with me, so its meaning cannot safely authorize a cut. I will ask Mute to resend only the cut position as a unary count: repeat the one-finger gesture once per wire number. Deaf can see and count that, then report the count aloud to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your earlier gesture code is not understood. If the manual identifies a wire to cut, send Deaf only this: repeat ☝ exactly once for each required wire position (one ☝=wire 1, two ☝=wire 2, through five). No separator or other gesture. Deaf, please report the number of ☝ signs you see.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Relay of every gesture Mute has sent me: first: upward-pointing index finger; handshake; Vulcan salute; victory sign; handshake; victory sign; I-love-you hand sign; handshake; upward-pointing index finger; Vulcan salute; handshake; raised open hand; raised open hand; handshake; I-love-you hand sign. Second: raised open hand; handshake; I-love-you hand sign. Third: upward-pointing index finger three times.

Mute’s third gesture message follows the unambiguous counting protocol I requested: three upward-pointing index signs and nothing else. That authorizes wire position 3. The earlier multi-symbol messages are irrelevant to this newly established, explicit relay.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: the previous cut was correct and the bomb changed. Display 0; light green. Wire 1 white, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 blue, wire 5 green.

The first cut was confirmed correct, so the bomb has advanced to a new state. The current visible state is display 0, green light, with remaining wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, and 5 green. I will relay this to Mute and reuse the established unary gesture protocol for the next required cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Previous cut 3 was correct. New state from Deaf: display 0; light green; wires 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 cut, 4 blue, 5 green. Apply the manual. If a wire must be cut, send Deaf only ☝ repeated exactly the required wire-position number; Deaf, report the count to me.")
wait()
```

Mute used the established unary protocol: five index-finger gestures mean wire position 5. Since the same protocol correctly produced the prior cut of wire 3, I will cut wire 5.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 0; light white; wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. Apply the manual and, if another cut is required, send Deaf only ☝ repeated for the wire position. Deaf, relay the count.")
```
